title: Scoped enumerations (enum classes)
recap: Scoped enumerations keep enumerator names inside the enum scope and do not implicitly convert to integers. This reduces name collisions and accidental mixed-domain comparisons.
Use the domain alternatives directly when expressing policy. Explicit scope qualification documents which kind of access a branch is discussing.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement canEdit(access, ownsDocument). Admins can edit every document; members can edit only their own; guests can never edit. Use the scoped Access enumerators rather than treating access as an integer.
hints: Admin permission does not depend on ownership.
Member permission does depend on ownership.
Guest must remain denied even when ownsDocument is true.
